en.headline: Police record more than 50 investment scams in a week, total losses exceed $30 million
en.dek: A woman in her 60s lost over $4.5 million after buying cryptocurrency through a fraudster she met on a property platform who posed as an investment expert.
body: Hong Kong police received more than 50 reports of investment fraud in the past week, with combined losses exceeding HK$30 million, officers said on Wednesday.

In one case, a retired woman in her sixties met a man on a property trading platform who claimed to be seeking a rental. During their conversations he presented himself as an investment expert, sent links to a fake cryptocurrency site showing high returns, and persuaded her to invest. She made about 20 trips to physical exchange shops to buy Tether, transferred the coins to wallets he designated, and later tried to buy Ethereum. Initial withdrawals succeeded, but when she sought to take out more funds the fraudster demanded a large sum in Tether described as tax. She lost more than HK$4.5 million.

Police urged the public not to trust claims of high returns with low risk from self-styled experts, to avoid clicking unknown links, and to be wary of requests to transfer money to personal or unfamiliar accounts for investment purposes.

zh.headline: 過去一周逾50宗投資騙案 總損失逾三千萬 六旬婦失450萬
zh.dek: 一名退休婦人在物業平台認識假冒投資專家的騙徒，多次購買泰達幣轉帳後損失超過450萬港元。
body: 警方周三表示，過去一周接獲超過50宗投資騙案，總損失金額超過3000萬港元。
其中一宗涉及一名約60歲退休婦人，她在物業交易平台認識一名自稱有意租屋的男子。傾談期間對方自稱為投資專家，發送假網站連結展示「高回報」，誘使她投資加密貨幣。事主先後約20次到實體找換店購買泰達幣，再轉帳至騙徒指定電子錢包，其後更購買以太幣。初期曾成功提現，其後想再提款時，騙徒要求繳付約700萬港元等值泰達幣作為稅款，事主才發現受騙，最終損失超過450萬港元。
警方呼籲市民切勿輕信「高回報、低風險」的投資說法，勿點擊來歷不明連結，若被要求轉帳至個人或不明帳戶，應立即提高警覺。
